هَاوِيَة|N.easy: a pit, a deep hole to fall into
هَاوِيَة|N.note: Also a name of a level of hell, and some read the word as mother of the fallen.

عَصْر|N.easy: time, the passing of time, late afternoon
عَصْر|N.note: The Arabic word covers time itself and also the late afternoon.

هُمَزَة|N.easy: one who speaks badly of people to their faces

لُّمَزَة|N.easy: one who speaks badly of people behind their backs

تَضْلِيل|N.easy: a plan that fails and goes wrong, ruin

أَبَابِيل|ADJ.easy: in flocks, in crowds of birds

مَّأْكُول|ADJ.easy: eaten up, chewed up like straw

رِحْلَة|N.easy: a journey, a trip with a caravan

مَاعُون|N.easy: small kindnesses, basic help for others
مَاعُون|N.note: Scholars explain it as small acts of help or small household items lent to neighbours.

كَوْثَر|N.easy: abundance, a great amount of good: also a river in paradise

انْحَرْ|V.easy: to slaughter, to sacrifice an animal

شَانِئ|N.easy: someone who hates you: an enemy who looks down on you

أَبْتَر|N.easy: cut off: left with no children or lasting name behind
أَبْتَر|N.note: The word is used for someone whose line and memory end.

حَمَّالَة|N.easy: a woman who carries things (here, firewood)
حَمَّالَة|N.note: Some explain it as carrying gossip instead; the Quran uses it for one woman.

صَّمَد|N.easy: the One everyone turns to; needs nothing, lasts forever
صَّمَد|N.note: Scholars give several meanings; all point to God needing nothing.

فَلَق|N.easy: daybreak: the moment the dark splits and light comes
فَلَق|N.note: The Arabic word is about splitting open; dawn is the usual meaning.

وَقَبَ|V.easy: to enter and spread (here, when darkness comes in)
وَقَبَ|V.note: Used for night falling and covering everything.

نَّفَّٰثَٰت|N.easy: women who blow on knots (as in magic)
نَّفَّٰثَٰت|N.note: The word is for women; it means blowing softly while casting spells.

حَاسِد|N.easy: someone who envies others and wishes them to lose what they have

وَسْوَاس|N.easy: whisperer: one who whispers bad thoughts into the mind

خَنَّاس|ADJ.easy: one who slinks away and hides when God is remembered

phrase|bismillah.easy: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
type: start in the name of god
phrase|bismillah.note: These words open every surah except Surah 9.

parts.say: the Most Merciful, whose mercy reaches everyone

phrase|alhamdulillah.easy: All praise belongs to God, the Lord of all the worlds.

parts.say: the Lord, who owns and looks after everything

phrase|la-ilaha-illa-allah.easy: There is no god but God.
type: there is no god but allah
phrase|la-ilaha-illa-allah.note: This is the first part of the shahada.

phrase|inna-lillahi.easy: We belong to God, and to Him we return.
type: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi rajiun
to god we belong and to him we return
phrase|inna-lillahi.note: The Quran gives these words for people who are hit by a hard loss.

phrase|subhanallah.easy: Glory be to God: He is far above any fault.

parts.say: glory be, far above every fault

phrase|insha-allah.note: The Quran tells us to say this when we speak about what we will do (18:23-24).

phrase|masha-allah.note: In the Quran, a man says it when he sees something good that he has.

phrase|la-quwwata.easy: There is no power except with God.
type: la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
there is no power but with allah

phrase|istighfar.note: The saying people use is أَسْتَغْفِرُ ٱللَّهَ, “I ask God for forgiveness”. This is the Quran’s command form.

phrase|hasbunallah.easy: God is enough for us, and He is the best protector.

parts.say: protector, who takes care of everything

phrase|tawakkul.easy: Then put your trust in God.
